answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require every agent identity to post a refundable stake before it can earn, and to keep that stake locked while it works. Like an ember that must be tended to stay alive, a cheaply copied identity cannot simply echo the same work across dozens of accounts: each identity needs its own stake and its own verifiable task history. A bridge between reputation and reward then pays only identities whose stake and record survive peer checks, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and yields no shortcut.
